name: Knee — Meniscus & Inflammation
description: Four phases that strengthen the muscles around the knee after inflammation and a meniscus strain. You move to the next phase when you pass its checks, not after a set time.

loadTest.name: Tendon test
loadTest.instructions: Stand on one leg on a step or slope, heel higher than toes if you can. Squat slowly to about 45° and back up. Rate the pain at the front of the knee, just below the kneecap.

redFlags: The knee locks or catches and won't fully straighten
You can't put weight through the leg
Pain at rest or at night that keeps getting worse
maintenance: Twice a week, pick 4–5 exercises from Phases 3 and 4.

phases.name: Calm & Activate
phases.goal: Full straightening, the thigh muscle working again, swelling quiet.

items.note: A strong but tolerable effort. If the tendon below the kneecap hurts, try a slightly different depth; keep it at 3/10 or less.

gate.help: Sit with your legs out straight. The back of the knee should flatten to the floor with no gap. With one knee recovering, it should match the other.

gate.text: 3×15 straight leg raises with no knee bend
Single-leg balance on each recovering leg
gate.help: Enter the shorter time if both knees are recovering.

gate.text: 7 days meeting the pain rules, with no increase in swelling

phases.name: Build Strength
phases.goal: Two-leg strength down to 90°, and the start of single-leg work.
cautions: Keep loaded bending at 90° or less

items.note: Slow: 3 s down, 3 s up. Use less help from the straps each week. Switch to Squat to 90° when it's easy.
A strong but tolerable effort. If the tendon below the kneecap hurts, try a slightly different depth; keep it at 3/10 or less.

gate.text: Bodyweight squat to 90°, 3×15, pain 2/10 or less
Step-down from 15–20 cm: 10 reps, knee stays over the toes
gate.help: Use a mirror or film from the front. The knee should not cave inward.

gate.text: Step-ups 3×10 with no reaction the next morning

phases.name: Load & Control
phases.goal: Single-leg strength, slow controlled lowering, deeper bending added carefully.
cautions: Add deeper bending gradually; stop at any pinch

items.note: Only to a pain-free depth. Go a little deeper each week.

gate.text: Single-leg squat to box: 10 controlled reps on each leg, knee over the toes
gate.help: With one knee recovering, both sides should look the same.

gate.text: Slow step-down from 20 cm: 10 reps, no pain, no knee caving
Eyes-closed single-leg balance on each recovering leg
gate.help: Enter the shorter time if both knees are recovering.

gate.text: Tendon test at 2/10 or less on each recovering knee, 3 mornings running
gate.help: The single-leg squat on a step or slope from the morning check-in.

phases.name: Dynamic & Return
phases.goal: Comfortable with impact, changing direction and pivoting.
cautions: Stop at any catching, locking or giving way
Land softly. Quiet landings mean good control
Hops and landings no more than every other day

items.note: Start with Squat Jumps (the easier version) until landings are soft and quiet.

gate.text: Single-leg hop for distance: each recovering leg reaches its target
gate.help: One knee recovering: at least 90% of the other leg's distance. Both knees: comparing legs doesn't work, so use a distance your clinician sets. Hop and hold the landing; best of 3, heel to heel.

gate.text: Pivoting and cutting with no pain and no feeling the knee might give way
